note: Numeric ranges, codes and names come from the BJCP 2021 Beer Style Guidelines; summaries are written for BrewNotes and are not guideline text.

styles.name: American Light Lager
styles.summary: Very pale, very light-bodied lager built for refreshment: minimal malt, barely-there hops and a crisp, dry finish.

styles.name: American Lager
styles.summary: Pale, clean and highly carbonated lager with a touch more body and malt than the light version, still restrained in hops.

styles.name: Cream Ale
styles.summary: Clean, pale American ale brewed and conditioned like a lager; light corn-like sweetness with a smooth, easy finish.

styles.name: American Wheat Beer
styles.summary: Light, refreshing wheat beer with a clean yeast character rather than banana and clove; often hazy with a soft grainy flavour.

styles.name: International Pale Lager
styles.summary: Highly attenuated pale lager with a little more flavour than the American mass-market versions; balanced and easy drinking.

styles.name: International Amber Lager
styles.summary: Smooth amber lager with a gentle caramel or toasty malt note and low bitterness; made for broad appeal.

styles.name: International Dark Lager
styles.summary: Dark but light-bodied lager with restrained roast and some sweetness; colour comes more from dark malt than flavour.

styles.name: Czech Pale Lager
styles.summary: Lower-strength Czech lager with soft bready malt, Saaz hop character and a rounded, somewhat bitter finish.

styles.name: Czech Premium Pale Lager
styles.summary: The classic Czech pilsner: rich, soft pale malt, pronounced Saaz hop flavour and a long, clean bitterness.

styles.name: Czech Amber Lager
styles.summary: Malty amber Czech lager with bready, caramel and toasty notes and moderate hop bitterness; richer than its pale sibling.

styles.name: Czech Dark Lager
styles.summary: Dark Czech lager that can run from sweet and roasty to dry and bitter; smooth, complex malt with a soft body.

styles.name: Munich Helles
styles.summary: Pale, malt-forward German lager with a soft, bready sweetness and just enough hop bitterness to keep it clean.

styles.name: Festbier
styles.summary: Golden, smooth and malty celebration lager, a bit stronger than Helles, with a clean toasty-bready character.

styles.name: Helles Bock
styles.summary: Strong pale German lager, rich in bready malt with low hop flavour and a clean, well-attenuated finish.

styles.name: German Leichtbier
styles.summary: Light-bodied, lower-alcohol German pale lager with a crisp hop bitterness relative to its gentle malt.

styles.name: Kölsch
styles.summary: Delicate, brilliant pale ale from Cologne fermented cool and lagered; subtle fruit, soft malt and a crisp dry finish.

styles.name: German Helles Exportbier
styles.summary: Pale, well-balanced German lager a touch stronger and fuller than Pils, with firm malt and moderate hop bitterness.

styles.name: German Pils
styles.summary: Crisp, dry and bitter pale German lager with floral or spicy noble hops over a light, clean grainy malt.

styles.name: Märzen
styles.summary: Amber, toasty German lager with rich bready malt, low bitterness and a smooth, dry finish; the traditional Oktoberfest beer.

styles.name: Rauchbier
styles.summary: Amber Franconian lager with a beechwood smoked-malt character layered over Märzen-like toasty malt.

styles.name: Dunkles Bock
styles.summary: Dark, strong and very malty German lager with toasty, bready richness and little hop presence.

styles.name: Vienna Lager
styles.summary: Amber-red lager with an elegant toasty malt flavour, moderate body and a clean, dry, lightly bitter finish.

styles.name: Altbier
styles.summary: Copper-coloured, bitter German ale fermented cool and lagered; clean, with firm bitterness and smooth malt.

styles.name: Munich Dunkel
styles.summary: Dark Munich lager with deep bready, toasty malt flavours, no roast harshness and gentle hop bitterness.

styles.name: Schwarzbier
styles.summary: Black lager that drinks lighter than it looks: gentle roast, bready malt and a dry, clean finish.

styles.name: Doppelbock
styles.summary: Strong, intensely malty German lager ranging from pale to dark; rich, bready and warming with low bitterness.

styles.name: Eisbock
styles.summary: Very strong, concentrated bock made by freezing and removing ice; intensely malty, rich and warming.

styles.name: Baltic Porter
styles.summary: Strong, smooth dark lager with layered toffee, dark fruit and gentle roast flavours and a clean fermentation.

styles.name: Weissbier
styles.summary: Pale Bavarian wheat beer with banana and clove from the yeast, a fluffy body and lively carbonation.

styles.name: Dunkles Weissbier
styles.summary: Darker, maltier take on Weissbier with bready caramel notes alongside the banana and clove character.

styles.name: Weizenbock
styles.summary: Strong Bavarian wheat beer, pale or dark, with rich malt, yeast-driven fruit and spice and a warming strength.

styles.name: Ordinary Bitter
styles.summary: Low-strength, session-strength English ale with hop bitterness balancing a light bready or biscuity malt.

styles.name: Best Bitter
styles.summary: Flavourful English bitter of moderate strength with more malt and hop character than the ordinary version.

styles.name: Strong Bitter
styles.summary: Stronger, fuller English bitter with a firm hop bitterness and a malt backbone that can show caramel notes.

styles.name: British Golden Ale
styles.summary: Pale, hop-forward British ale with a light malt base and a crisp, refreshing bitterness.

styles.name: Australian Sparkling Ale
styles.summary: Pale, highly carbonated Australian ale with a fruity yeast note, firm bitterness and a dry finish.

styles.name: English IPA
styles.summary: Hoppy, bitter and moderately strong pale English ale with a dry finish and earthy or floral English hops.

styles.name: Dark Mild
styles.summary: Low-strength dark English ale that is malty and gentle, with chocolate or caramel flavours and little bitterness.

styles.name: British Brown Ale
styles.summary: Malty, nutty brown ale of moderate strength with caramel and toffee notes and restrained hopping.

styles.name: English Porter
styles.summary: Moderate-strength dark English ale with chocolate and caramel malt flavours and a soft, drinkable character.

styles.name: Scottish Light
styles.summary: Lowest-strength Scottish ale: malty, a little caramel, low bitterness and a clean finish.

styles.name: Scottish Heavy
styles.summary: Malt-focused Scottish session ale with a bit more body and strength than Light, still gentle on hops.

styles.name: Scottish Export
styles.summary: Fullest of the Scottish ales, with rich caramel malt, moderate strength and a clean, low-hop profile.

styles.name: Irish Red Ale
styles.summary: Easy-drinking amber-red ale with a light caramel and toasty malt flavour and a dry, roasted-grain finish.

styles.name: Irish Stout
styles.summary: Dry, roasty black ale with a coffee-like bitterness, creamy texture and modest strength.

styles.name: Irish Extra Stout
styles.summary: Fuller, stronger version of Irish stout with more roast, dark chocolate and a richer body.

styles.name: Sweet Stout
styles.summary: Dark, sweet and full-bodied stout, often with lactose, giving a smooth, dessert-like roast character.

styles.name: Oatmeal Stout
styles.summary: Smooth, full-bodied dark ale where oats add silkiness alongside gentle roast and some sweetness.

styles.name: Tropical Stout
styles.summary: Sweet, fruity stout from warm climates, moderately strong with low bitterness and a smooth roast.

styles.name: Foreign Extra Stout
styles.summary: Strong, roasty export stout, from dry to moderately sweet, with coffee and dark chocolate flavours.

styles.name: British Strong Ale
styles.summary: Malty, moderately strong English ale, often rich with caramel and dark fruit and a balancing bitterness.

styles.name: Old Ale
styles.summary: Aged, strong English ale with malt complexity, dried fruit and sometimes a hint of oxidation or wood.

styles.name: Wee Heavy
styles.summary: Strong, rich Scottish ale dominated by caramel and toffee malt with a warming, smooth finish.

styles.name: English Barleywine
styles.summary: Very strong, complex English ale with intense malt, dried fruit and a long, warming, often aged character.

styles.name: Blonde Ale
styles.summary: Light, approachable American pale ale with soft malt, restrained hops and a clean, easy finish.

styles.name: American Pale Ale
styles.summary: Pale, refreshing American ale showing citrusy or piney hops over a clean, light malt base with moderate bitterness.

styles.name: American Amber Ale
styles.summary: Amber American ale balancing caramel malt against citrusy American hops and a moderate bitterness.

styles.name: California Common
styles.summary: Amber beer fermented with lager yeast at ale temperatures; toasty malt, woody Northern Brewer hops and a clean finish.

styles.name: American Brown Ale
styles.summary: Malty brown ale with chocolate and caramel notes, given a hoppier, more bitter edge than its British cousin.

styles.name: American Porter
styles.summary: Robust, roasty dark ale with chocolate flavours and a noticeable American hop presence.

styles.name: American Stout
styles.summary: Strong, bold stout with assertive roast and American hop bitterness and flavour.

styles.name: Imperial Stout
styles.summary: Very strong, intense black ale with layers of roast, dark fruit and chocolate and a warming finish.

styles.name: American IPA
styles.summary: Hop-forward pale ale with prominent citrus, pine or tropical American hops, firm bitterness and a dry finish.

styles.name: Specialty IPA
styles.summary: A family of IPAs that change one major element of the American IPA, such as colour, grain or yeast; ranges depend on the variant.

variants.name: Belgian IPA
variants.summary: IPA fermented with Belgian yeast, adding fruity, spicy esters and phenols to a hop-forward base.

variants.name: Black IPA
variants.summary: Dark IPA with the hop intensity of an American IPA and only a gentle roast; drinks like an IPA, looks like a stout.

variants.name: Brown IPA
variants.summary: Hoppy IPA with the caramel and chocolate malt flavours of a brown ale underneath.

variants.name: Brut IPA
variants.summary: Very dry, pale and highly carbonated IPA with low bitterness and expressive hop aroma, often using enzymes to dry out.

variants.name: Red IPA
variants.summary: IPA with a red-amber colour and caramel malt depth supporting bold American hops.

variants.name: Rye IPA
variants.summary: IPA with a noticeable share of rye, adding a spicy, drying grain character to the hops.

variants.name: White IPA
variants.summary: Hoppy cross between an American IPA and a Belgian witbier: wheat, spices and citrus hops.

styles.name: Hazy IPA
styles.summary: Soft, juicy, cloudy IPA with intense tropical and citrus hop aroma, low perceived bitterness and a full, smooth body.

styles.name: Double IPA
styles.summary: Stronger, more intensely hopped IPA that stays drinkable: big hop flavour and bitterness with a dry finish.

styles.name: American Strong Ale
styles.summary: Strong, malty and hoppy American ale that sits between an amber ale and a barleywine.

styles.name: American Barleywine
styles.summary: Very strong American ale with intense malt and an equally bold, citrusy hop presence.

styles.name: Wheatwine
styles.summary: Strong American ale built on wheat malt, bready and smooth with moderate hopping and honey-like richness.

styles.name: Berliner Weisse
styles.summary: Very pale, tart and light German wheat beer with a clean lactic sourness and low alcohol.

styles.name: Flanders Red Ale
styles.summary: Sour, fruity red-brown Belgian ale aged in wood, with tart cherry, plum and a touch of vinegar-like acidity.

styles.name: Oud Bruin
styles.summary: Malty, lightly sour brown Belgian ale with caramel, dark fruit and a gentle tartness from long aging.

styles.name: Lambic
styles.summary: Unblended, spontaneously fermented Belgian wheat beer: tart, funky and complex, usually served young and flat.

styles.name: Gueuze
styles.summary: Blend of young and old lambic refermented in the bottle: effervescent, tart, funky and complex.

styles.name: Fruit Lambic
styles.summary: Lambic refermented with fruit such as cherries or raspberries, balancing tartness and fruit character.

styles.name: Gose
styles.summary: Tart, lightly salted German wheat beer with coriander and a refreshing, highly carbonated character.

styles.name: Witbier
styles.summary: Pale, hazy Belgian wheat beer spiced with coriander and orange peel; soft, refreshing and lightly tart.

styles.name: Belgian Pale Ale
styles.summary: Moderate-strength Belgian ale with toasty, biscuity malt, gentle fruit from the yeast and balanced hops.

styles.name: Bière de Garde
styles.summary: French farmhouse-style ale, malty and smooth, from blond to brown, with a clean, cellar-aged character.

styles.name: Belgian Blond Ale
styles.summary: Moderately strong golden Belgian ale with a soft malt sweetness, fruity-spicy yeast and a dry finish.

styles.name: Saison
styles.summary: Highly attenuated, dry and refreshing Belgian farmhouse ale with spicy, fruity yeast character; brewed at several strengths.

styles.name: Belgian Golden Strong Ale
styles.summary: Pale, strong, highly carbonated Belgian ale that is dry and deceptively light with fruity, spicy yeast notes.

styles.name: Belgian Single
styles.summary: Pale, hoppy and dry Belgian monastic table beer with a spicy yeast character and modest strength.

styles.name: Belgian Dubbel
styles.summary: Deep reddish-brown Belgian ale with rich malt, dark fruit and spicy yeast notes and a dry finish.

styles.name: Belgian Tripel
styles.summary: Strong golden Belgian ale, spicy and fruity from the yeast, with a light body and a dry, effervescent finish.

styles.name: Belgian Dark Strong Ale
styles.summary: Rich, complex, very strong dark Belgian ale with dark fruit, malt depth and spicy yeast character.

styles.name: Historical Beer
styles.summary: Beers of historical interest that are brewed today in small numbers; each named style below has its own profile.

variants.name: Kellerbier
variants.summary: Unfiltered, lightly carbonated version of a German lager served fresh from the cellar; ranges follow the base style.

variants.name: Kentucky Common
variants.summary: Dark amber American ale brewed quickly with corn and some dark malt; grainy and gently sweet.

variants.name: Lichtenhainer
variants.summary: Pale, tart and lightly smoked German wheat beer of low strength.

variants.name: London Brown Ale
variants.summary: Sweet, dark and low-alcohol English brown ale with caramel and toffee flavours.

variants.name: Piwo Grodziskie
variants.summary: Pale, low-alcohol Polish ale made from oak-smoked wheat malt; light, crisp and highly carbonated.

variants.name: Pre-Prohibition Lager
variants.summary: Fuller-flavoured American pilsner of the 1800s with corn or rice and a noticeable hop bitterness.

variants.name: Pre-Prohibition Porter
variants.summary: American porter of the 1800s with adjuncts and a lighter, drier roast than English versions.

variants.name: Roggenbier
variants.summary: German rye ale fermented with wheat beer yeast; spicy rye with banana and clove notes.

variants.name: Sahti
variants.summary: Traditional Finnish ale flavoured with juniper and often fermented with baker's yeast; strong, sweet and unusual.

styles.name: Brett Beer
styles.summary: Beer fermented wholly or partly with Brettanomyces, adding fruity, funky complexity; ranges follow the base style.

styles.name: Mixed-Fermentation Sour Beer
styles.summary: Sour beer fermented with a mix of yeast and bacteria; tart and complex, with ranges set by the base style.

styles.name: Wild Specialty Beer
styles.summary: Wild or sour beer with added fruit, spices, wood or other specialty ingredients; ranges follow the base style.

styles.name: Straight Sour Beer
styles.summary: Clean, soured beer without funk, usually quick-soured with Lactobacillus; bright acidity on a light base.

styles.name: Fruit Beer
styles.summary: Any base beer with fruit added as a noticeable but balanced component; ranges follow the base style.

styles.name: Fruit and Spice Beer
styles.summary: Beer combining fruit with spices, herbs or vegetables on a base style; ranges follow the base.

styles.name: Specialty Fruit Beer
styles.summary: Fruit beer with a further specialty ingredient such as sugar, honey or syrup; ranges follow the base style.

styles.name: Grape Ale
styles.summary: Beer brewed with a significant share of grapes or grape must, bridging beer and wine; varies with the grapes and base.

styles.name: Spice, Herb, or Vegetable Beer
styles.summary: Beer with spices, herbs or vegetables in supporting balance with a base style; ranges follow the base.

styles.name: Autumn Seasonal Beer
styles.summary: Autumn-themed spiced beer, often pumpkin-pie flavoured and amber in colour; usually above session strength.

styles.name: Winter Seasonal Beer
styles.summary: Spiced, often dark and stronger winter beer suggesting the flavours of the holiday season.

styles.name: Specialty Spice Beer
styles.summary: Spiced beer that also features another specialty ingredient such as sugar or honey; ranges follow the base.

styles.name: Alternative Grain Beer
styles.summary: Beer where an unusual grain such as oats, rye, buckwheat or spelt is a defining ingredient; ranges follow the base.

styles.name: Alternative Sugar Beer
styles.summary: Beer where an added sugar such as honey, maple or molasses is a defining ingredient; ranges follow the base.

styles.name: Classic Style Smoked Beer
styles.summary: A classic style with smoked malt added; the smoke complements rather than overwhelms the base beer.

styles.name: Specialty Smoked Beer
styles.summary: Smoked beer on a non-classic base or with additional specialty ingredients.

styles.name: Wood-Aged Beer
styles.summary: Beer aged in or on wood without strong spirit character; wood and vanilla notes over the base style.

styles.name: Specialty Wood-Aged Beer
styles.summary: Beer aged in barrels that held spirits or wine, picking up flavours from the previous contents.

styles.name: Commercial Specialty Beer
styles.summary: A beer brewed to match a specific commercial style not otherwise described in the guidelines.

styles.name: Mixed-Style Beer
styles.summary: A beer that deliberately combines two or more classic styles.

styles.name: Experimental Beer
styles.summary: Beer using ingredients, processes or ideas that fit no other category; anything goes, within reason.
